what: The tropical bank as stored in Neon (project Energylake), every row of the four tables the routes read, as Postgres's own row_to_json(t)::text, one row per line, in key order. Read-only through the Neon connector, 2026-10-09 22:08-22:11Z.
cut_rule: tropical_storms as read at 22:08:10Z (its max(updated_ts) is the cut; no storm row was updated after it); tropical_track_points and tropical_place_odds with inserted_ts <= cut; heartbeat rows of tropical_file_vintage with fetch_ts <= cut. Those three tables are insert-only (points and odds ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; a heartbeat row is never updated), so every chunk read the same rows.

heartbeat.columns: vintage_id, dataset, source, product, storm_id, vintage_key, status, fetch_ts, issued_ts, meta (WHERE product = 'heartbeat')

dataset.columns: dataset_code, lifecycle_status, refresh_cron, freshness_mode, stale_after_override, enabled (nhc_storms_current, tc_model_tracks)

sha256_rule: Neon computed encode(sha256(convert_to(string_agg(row_to_json(t)::text, E'\n' ORDER BY <order>), 'UTF8')), 'hex') in one statement at the cut; the suite recomputes it over the decompressed file (no trailing newline) on every load.
chunks: points in 7 reads (ntile over point_id), odds and heartbeats in one; bank_from_neon.py reassembled them and checked every sha before writing
